newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank surge boosts Australia stocks to record close.
newsitem.headline: Bank surge boosts Australia stocks to record close.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.305 -0.025 Gold NY 342.95 Lon fix 343.00
*No U.S. rate hike sparks banks rebound, boosts market to record close despite resources profit-taking. Volume 364 million, value A$884 million, 1092 stocks traded, 344 steady, 456 up, 292 down.
A resurgent banking sector, encouraged by news of no U.S. rate hike, carried the Australian stock market to a new record close on Wednesday.
"Buyers were coming back into the market looking for a bargain, in particular the banks," Reynolds and Co broker Peter Struk said.

National Australia Bank jumped 38 cents to A$18.18, leading a bank-wide rally which pushed the banks and finance index up 83.3 points or 1.92 percent to 4,432.9. This drove the All Ordinaries Index to finish 12.5 points higher to 2,543.2, up from the previous record close set of 2,538.1 set on May 16.
Fears about the profit effects of a squeeze on Australian lending margins had pushed the banks index down almost five percent in the past week from a May 13 closing high of 4,562.1.
Brokers said investors buoyant after the U.S. Federal Reserve's inaction and the Dow's rise on Tuesday rushed in to snap up banking stocks, seen as undervalued after their week-long slide.
Resources stocks, which had benefitted from switching away from the banks in the past week, were steady to lower as profit-takers moved in.
The All Resources Index closed down 4.2 points at 1,480.7.

Broken Hill Pty Co, which has risen over seven percent in the last week on the banks-to-resources switch, closed 11 cents down at A$19.15 having leapt in early trade to a new year high of A$19.41. CRA closed unchanged at A$21.12, having earlier risen to a year high of A$21.18.

Late morning wages data described by Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith as too high for a low inflation climate helped take the shine off the initial rally, but was eventually overwhelmed by a basically bullish market.
The local bond market sold off after private wages data for the March quarter showed 4.8 percent growth.
The 10 year bond yield closed up two basis points at 7.68 percent after the wages data disappointed bond-holders hoping for another local rate cut.
Highlights amoung the smaller stocks included the 17 cent rise by whitegoods maker Email Ltd to A$4.05 after a five week strike at its Martin Bright steel plant ended.
Industrial services group Campbell Brothers rose 36 cents to A$5.01 after a strong profit result late on Tuesday.
Cigarette maker Rothmans jumped 70 cents or 8.4 percent to a new high of A$9.00 after it announced a doubling of annual profits and posted a A$1.00 per share special dividend.
Burns Philp & Co fell another eight cents to A$1.79 as investors voted with their feet over the food group's plan to sell off its spice assets in an attempt to restore profits.
The appetite for shares in just-floated bancassurance group Colonial Ltd appeared yet to be exhausted, as the stock rose two cents to A$3.38 on volume of over almost six million.

Woodside Petroleum weakened again as recent talk of a potential takeover continued to evaporate. It fell nine cents to A$10.85, having fallen 24 cents on Tuesday. The Australian dollar closed up at US$0.7764 from its US$0.7713 low offshore, helped by a bounce in US$/yen and the firm wages data.
